title: Routing & Auth Triage + Playbook (working draft)
content:
Meeting: Platform Engineering - Routing/Auth triage + playbook workshop (working notes)
Date: 2026-02-20
Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Duration: 40m (weekly ad-hoc)

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Miguel Santos
- Rina Koh
- Jared Lin
- Priya Desai
- Guests: Samir (SRE - on-call) joined for first 15m

Goal: capture recurring incident patterns for routing/auth/quotas, prioritize runbook steps, and list concrete action items to reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) and avoid manual fallbacks. Leave with a draft playbook we can iterate in next 2 sprints.

High-level summary / quick hits:
- Observed 3x small routing congestion incidents in last 3 weeks — common pattern: abrupt spike + slow drain when queries use large KV cache sets. (PLT-3456 referenced)
- Auth token refresh latencies spiking intermittently during region failovers; correlated with external KMS latency (Auth trace sample attached in linked PR).
- Quota throttling behavior is generally OK but opaque to dev teams; need clearer metrics and per-customer SLO dashboards.

Agenda items and notes:
1) Incident patterns & reproducibility
   - Miguel: reproduced routing slow-drain locally with a synthetic workload that alternates long-context and short-context requests. Root cause hypothesis: allocator fragmentation + batching window interaction.
   - Rina: noted that kernel selection sometimes switches mid-stream when sequence length changes; that can extend CPU-side scheduling. File bug in infra scheduling (LINK: PLT-3599).
   - Action: Miguel + Jared to produce minimal repro harness by 2026-02-27 and open a targeted perf PR. Owner: Miguel.

2) Auth token refresh spikes
   - Symptoms: 2 spikes last week where token refresh latency > 1200ms causing 504s for short-lived routes.
   - Triage: correlated with KMS region failover traces — fallback to remote KMS increased round trips.
   - Short-term mitigation: increase auth cache TTL to 45s for affected routes and enable aggressive local retry w/ jitter.
   - Long-term: integrate async refresh path to avoid blocking request threads. Owner: Priya. Deliverable: design doc by 2026-03-05.

3) Quotas transparency and dashboards
   - Problem: customers see opaque 429s; internal teams cannot see per-route token burn patterns easily.
   - Proposal: add a per-route rolling-1m token consumption metric + alert when > 80% of committed quota.
   - Action: Jared to prototype a Grafana panel and shared dashboard link. Target demo: 2026-02-28.

4) Playbook draft structure (brainstorm)
   - Triage checklist: initial checks (is KMS ok? are allocator logs showing pod eviction? are kv-cache sizes high?), quick mitigations, escalation matrix, rollback criteria.
   - Severity levels tied to customer impact and sustained error rate (S1/S2/S3); attach standard Slack templates.
   - Communication: prepare customer-facing snippet for S1 that the support team can paste into Zendesk.
   - Owner: Aisha to assemble first pass doc by 2026-02-24.

5) Automation opportunities
   - Auto-scale routing pools when sustained queue length > threshold for 30s — caveat: cost. Experiment flags needed.
   - Auto-fallback to compatible model variant on capacity pressure — use the existing routing policy layer, add a prioritized variant list.
   - Action: create RFC in repo (team will discuss sizing tradeoffs). Owner: Rina. RFC due: 2026-03-10.

Blockers & open questions:
- Can SRE grant a read-only view into the KMS health board for the platform team? (Samir to check)
- Should auth TTL changes be per-route or per-tenant? Need security review for replay surface. Open: Priya to get sec review owner.
- How aggressive should auto-scale be given current cost targets? Need input from finance/product.

Action items (concrete)
- PLT-3456: Miguel + Jared -> minimal repro harness & perf PR (due 2026-02-27)
- Auth-async: Priya -> design doc for async token refresh (due 2026-03-05)
- Dashboards: Jared -> Grafana panel + demo (due 2026-02-28)
- Playbook v0: Aisha -> assemble triage playbook + Slack templates (due 2026-02-24)
- RFC auto-scale: Rina -> write RFC for auto-scale + fallback policy (due 2026-03-10)
- Samir (SRE) -> confirm KMS board access for platform (update by 2026-02-23)

Notes-to-self / quick TODOs (choppy)
- drop-in sample curl commands for token-check in playbook (Jared)
- example log filters: "allocator.*evict" and "kv-cache.*size>" (Miguel)
- backup contact list for S1 on-call 😬 (Aisha)

References & links (working):
- Linear: PLT-3456 routing backpressure
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/981 (perf tracing additions)
- Internal trace sample: jira://AUTH-129

Meeting retro (what worked / what to change)
- + Good cross-team voice: SRE helped connect KMS patterns quickly.
- - Need clearer pre-meeting data: next time attach 1-2 flamegraphs + one timeline screenshot.
- Plan: keep this session monthly but spin up ad-hoc when incidents spike.

Next meeting: tentative 2026-03-06 (or earlier if PLT-3456 repro ready)

---
Draft playbook outline (appendix rough)
1) Runbook header: incident id, reported at, owner, severity, customers impacted
2) Quick checks: KMS health, routing-pool utilization, allocator error spikes, quota events, recent deploys
3) Immediate mitigations (0-10m): increase auth TTL, enable local retry, route fallback to variant, temporarily widen batching window
4) Mid-term mitigations (10-60m): scale routing pool, disable problematic node pool, roll back recent kernel-selection change
5) Escalation: contacts + Slack templates
6) Post-incident: timeline, RCA owner, perf follow-up actions, customer communications

End of notes.

(Working doc — iterate in repo under docs/triage/playbooks/routing-auth-playbook.md once v0 ready)
